issues.where: release_plan: `ok = in_arm & (sig <= m.n - 2)` and `ok &= xi > sig + 1`; signals: `if xi < m.n: s.exit_long[xi - 1] = True` / `s.exit_short[xi - 1] = True`
issues.issue: Two single-bar truncation points remain for every kept trade. A targeted sweep on the stage-0 EURUSD market (all 24 cells, 25 kept trades per cell) found prefix mismatches at every cut k = sig+1 (600 of 600; entry_long/entry_short and sl_dist on bar sig) and at every cut k = xi (600 of 600; exit_long/exit_short on bar xi-1). It found none at sig+2, mid-hold, xi-1 or xi+1 (0 of 600 each). Causes: the pre-registered rule 'skip if sig >= m.n - 1' together with R1, which reads m.ts[sig+1] through xi; and the time exit placed on bar xi-1, which needs bar xi to exist. Both use only whether the next bar exists and when it opens, never a price, calendar or COT value; every perturbation and ext-release probe is clean. They encode 'market order at the next open if that open is before the target' and 'close at the first tick at or after 20:30' in bar-indexed signals. The oracle modules m3_usd_bid and gotobi_short use the same pattern. This is not an information leak, and it does not trip the real gate: leak_report on the pipeline's own EURUSD market (end 2024-01-01) with the spec params passes all 15 checks (2 truncation, 4 perturbation, 1 determinism, 8 ext-release), and that run is deterministic.
issues.fix: No change needed for this run. If a later leak run (other params or another end date) ever places a probe exactly on one of these points, the signature is a mismatch confined to the last bar of the prefix: entry fields on bar k-1 = sig, or exit flags on bar k-1 = xi-1. Read that as this artefact, not as a leak. Optional hardening if the module is reused: gate the entry with sig <= m.n - 1 and evaluate R1 as close_times[sig] < target. That changes no trade, because R1 never binds through a data gap on any of the six markets (0 cases over 24 cells). Keep the exit encoding: it is the faithful clock exit, and a close-time marker would exit one bar late in the 7 cell-trades where a data gap spans 20:30.

issues.issue: Under the pre-registered same-UTC-date rule, every Japanese release at 23:50 UTC (08:50 JST: GDP, Tankan, trade balance, machinery orders) has its signal bar at 00:00 UTC on the next date and is skipped in every arm and both holds. Example: USDJPY against q0.8 z1.0 loses 2 of 76 design releases (2013-03-07, 2014-11-16). The code matches the rule as written. The effect is to thin USDJPY quote-side (JPY) news, which breadth rule (3) splits on.
issues.fix: No code change; the rule is pre-registered. The Director should note it when reading the USDJPY news-side split.

lookahead_risk: Low. Every value at the signal bar uses bars up to that bar's close, calendar rows with ts_avail <= T, the COT row with ts_avail <= T (its 52-row rank uses only rows up to it), and ATR20 known at the day start. The perturbation probes, which move prices, calendar numbers and COT numbers after the cut, are all clean. The only forward dependency is at clock level: whether the next bar exists and when it opens (k = sig+1 and k = xi, first issue), with no price content. The Builder's R1 deviation removes a much larger dependency that my note 5 would have created: the literal xi < m.n gate made the entry depend on data up to three days after the signal bar. A scratch copy with that gate fails stage 0 on the real primary market (ext-release cut 2022-01-05 13:30, 178 mismatches from bar 299656 in entry_long, sl_dist and the previous trade's exit flags) and fails the checker slice; the submitted module passes both.
notes: VERDICT ON THE DEVIATION: correct, and required by the contract. My note 5 was wrong on this point. The literal gate (keep only if xi < m.n) keeps an entry only if a bar exists at the exit target. That makes the entry flag at bar sig depend on bars up to three days later, which is look-ahead by the contract's own truncation test. I reproduced the stage-0 failure the Builder reported. The deviation changes no trade in stages 0-C: over 6 markets x 24 cells, with markets cut at 2024-01-01 as the pipeline does, no kept release has its target past the last bar, so the trades are identical to the literal rule. The holdout has none either, because the calendar ends 2025-04-07 while bars run into 2026. If such a trade ever occurs, the executor closes it at the last bar's close (END), the engine's standard treatment. The primary marker is still placed only when bar xi exists, as the Director describes, and the docstring's CAUSALITY paragraph is accurate. Every SIGNAL exit is on bar xi, and there are no END exits. (3) NZDUSD d0: R1 removes exactly 14/10/22 against/with/neutral design releases (the 21:45 and 22:45 UTC prints); it never binds for d1. (4) The few one-bar trades (at most 2 per cell) are 1 x ATR stop-outs right after big prints (for example GBPUSD on US CPI 2018-01-12, USDCAD on NFP 2013-12-06), plus one rule-correct RBNZ 20:00 d0 trade exited at 20:30.
